the oscillating CO reaction on Pt nanofacet tips is a self-sustained process which is driven by a feedback mechanism between the reaction and the surface reconstruction of the Pt nanofaceted tip.
the oscillations in the reaction on Pt [1 1] and [1 0] facets are driven by the reconstruction feedback mechanism and that the [1 1]-facet is the main active site.
oscillations in CO oxidation on a Pt nanofacet are caused by the reconstruction feedback mechanism.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reconstruction feedback loop is the key mechanism for the global oscillations of the CO oxidation on Pt.

the oscillatory behaviour of CO oxidation on Pt is a result of a complex interplay of different surface reactions and surface diffusion processes, which are influenced by the crystallographic orientation of the Pt surface and the surface structure.
the reconstruction feedback loop, as a mechanism for self-oscillation of the CO oxidation reaction, is also valid at nm-sized particles with their different crystallographic orientation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oscillating reaction is governed by the same principles in the macroscopic and microscopic systems.
the CO adsorption on the Pt surface is the key factor in the oscillation mechanism.
we have shown that oscillations on a Pt nanotip are not only possible but also very similar to the ones on macroscopic Pt single crystals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oscillations are not only observed in the CO coverage on the [1 1] and [1 1 1] facets, but also on the [1 0 0] facets.
the reconstruction feedback loop is a general mechanism for self-sustained oscillatory reactions on Pt nanofacet surfaces.
the reconstruction feedback is a general phenomenon for all crystallographic orientations, even for the smallest ones.
